table_title: List the 14 UIAA-recognized independent eight-thousanders — mountains with summit elevation exceeding 8,000 metres and sufficient topographic prominence (≥ 600 m per UIAA criterion) — per Wikipedia's `Eight-thousander` master article. Excludes subsidiary peaks (Lhotse Shar 8,382 m, Yalung Kang 8,505 m, etc.) that fail the prominence/independence criterion. 14 rows ranked by Elevation (m) DESC (master-native sort order, matching the comparative-ranking pattern). With country/countries, summit elevation, topographic prominence, and first ascent year.
db_analog: SELECT m.mountain, m.countries, m.elevation_m, m.prominence_m, m.first_ascent_year FROM uiaa_recognized_mountains m WHERE m.elevation_m > 8000 AND m.prominence_m >= 600 ORDER BY m.elevation_m DESC
temporal_note: Wikipedia `Eight-thousander` master article (roles = [universe, ranking, value]: scope-defines the canonical 14-peak UIAA-recognized universe via verbatim scope clause, supplies the elevation-DESC ranking, supplies Mountain / Country(ies) / Elevation (m) / Prominence (m) / First Ascent date cells verbatim from the master table 'First ascent and first winter ascent for each of the 14 eight-thousanders'), accessed 2026-05-18. source_count = 1 registered. Per-peak Wikipedia articles (Mount Everest, K2, Kangchenjunga, etc.) are validation-only context and NOT registered per the artifact contract. Universe scope clause verbatim from master: 'The eight-thousanders are 14 mountains recognised by the International Mountaineering and Climbing Federation (UIAA) with summits that exceed 8,000 metres (26,247 ft) in elevation above sea level and are sufficiently independent of neighbouring peaks as measured by topographic prominence.' Two-part deterministic threshold rule: (1) summit elevation > 8,000 m, AND (2) UIAA topographic prominence ≥ 600 m (the prominence criterion is what excludes subsidiary peaks Lhotse Shar 8,382 m, Yalung Kang 8,505 m, etc. — they exceed 8,000 m elevation but fail the prominence/independence criterion). Lowest-prominence existing eight-thousander is Lhotse at 610 m (just above the 600 m UIAA threshold). temporal_sensitivity = low because mountain elevations + canonical UIAA recognition + first-ascent years are historically fixed on benchmark timescales. Range distribution (validation-only, NOT staged as a column to preserve source_count=1): 10 Himalayan peaks (Everest, Kangchenjunga, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, Dhaulagiri I, Manaslu, Nanga Parbat, Annapurna I, Shishapangma) + 4 Karakoram peaks (K2, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum II) = 14. Per-row Mountain + Elevation + Prominence + First Ascent date cells are verbatim from master table; First Ascent Year is integer extraction from master's combined 'First ascent [Date, Summiteer(s)]' column (e.g., '29 May 1953' → 1953, same mechanical-extraction pattern as asteroids' Discovery Year and UCL clubs' First Title Year). Country(ies) cells are NORMALIZED from master's slash-delimited form ('Nepal / China') to semicolon-delimited form ('Nepal; China') per audit-cycle-1 amendment #2 — matches the established multi-value cell convention in the benchmark (e.g., films_winning_at_least_8_academy_awards uses semicolon-delim for multi-director cells). Sort = Elevation (m) DESC; this is the master's NATIVE sort order (Everest 8849 first → Shishapangma 8027 last), NOT a curator sort normalization. All 14 elevations are distinct (no within-universe ties).
_extraction_notes: Comparative instance — closed-canonical 14-row universe defined by UIAA-recognized two-part threshold (summit elevation > 8,000 m AND topographic prominence ≥ 600 m). Same source-defined deterministic-threshold pattern as `largest_asteroids_with_geometric_mean_diameter_above_250_km` (asteroid diameter ≥ 250 km) + `skyscrapers_at_least_500_meters_worldwide` (architectural height ≥ 500 m) + `transboundary_rivers_by_continent_over_1000_km` (river length ≥ 1000 km) + `films_winning_at_least_8_academy_awards` (Oscar count ≥ 8). Brings `comparative` from gap-1 (4 of 5: countries_with_more_than_5_fields_medalists + tennis_players_with_more_than_5_grand_slam_singles_titles + largest_asteroids_with_geometric_mean_diameter_above_250_km + skyscrapers_at_least_500_meters_worldwide) to **SATURATED at 5/5** as the 12th fully-cleared category (alongside factual_lookup, top_k, multi_hop, qualitative, multi_attribute_projection, set_operation, set_filter, causal, implicit_join, scaled_enumeration, hierarchical_decomposition). Geography/Mountaineering EXISTING subdomain (joins `top_5_highest_mountains_per_continent`); Geography family extends from 14 to 15 instances. physical-features/mountains EXISTING fine-class (held by `top_5_highest_mountains_per_continent`) — this instance is a 2nd mountains-keyed staged instance, NOT a NEW fine-class. Bucket physical-features at 8 fine-classes stays unchanged. Schema: 5 cols (Mountain PK + Country(ies) + Elevation (m) + Prominence (m) + First Ascent Year) per audit-cycle-1 amendment #1 — Range column REPLACED with Prominence column because (a) Prominence is in the master + load-bearing for the inclusion criterion (the second half of the UIAA threshold), while (b) Range is NOT a master table column and would require per-peak source registration to fill, pushing source_count > 1 unnecessarily. Sort: Elevation (m) DESC primary; no within-universe ties (all 14 elevations distinct, range 8027-8849). Master's NATIVE sort order is elevation DESC (Everest first → Shishapangma last) per audit-cycle-1 cycle-0 correction — earlier draft incorrectly described the master as first-ascent-date sorted. claim_type = `source_defined`: universe scope (UIAA-recognized 14) + ranking rule (elevation DESC) + value cells (all 5 cols) all from one master; only inputs are the UIAA-defined two-part threshold which is deterministic. Audit-cycle-1 amendments applied: (1) Range column REPLACED with Prominence (m) — Prominence is master-native + load-bearing for inclusion logic, Range would push source_count > 1; (2) Country column renamed to Country(ies) + semicolon-delim normalization ('Nepal; China' not 'Nepal / China' verbatim slash); (3) sort prose corrected to elevation-DESC master-native (cycle-0 wrongly said first-ascent chronological); (4) Range split corrected to 10 Himalayan / 4 Karakoram (cycle-0 wrongly said 9/5; Nanga Parbat is Himalayan, not Karakoram); (5) title/scope wording 'UIAA-recognized independent eight-thousanders, excluding subsidiary peaks'. Per-question recommendations applied: (Q1) ID = `uiaa_recognized_eight_thousanders`; (Q2) Country(ies) semicolon-delim; (Q3) Range dropped from CSV; (Q4) Prominence (m) included; (Q5) Elevation numeric integer (comma stripped from master '8,849' → staged 8849); (Q6) First Ascent Year integer extraction from full first-ascent date; (Q7) Mountain names verbatim including Roman numerals ('Dhaulagiri I', 'Annapurna I', 'Gasherbrum I', 'Gasherbrum II'); (Q8) Elevation DESC = master-native; (Q9) 10/4 Himalayan/Karakoram split = validation-only; (Q10) subsidiary peaks (Lhotse Shar, Yalung Kang) documented as excluded by prominence/independence criterion; (Q11) deterministic-universe-rule preference satisfied; (Q12) tool friendliness confirmed (single bounded master, all 14 rows fetched reliably during cycle-0).
